name: Swarovski Kristallwelten
kurzbeschreibung: Swarovski Crystal Worlds in Wattens dazzles visitors with 18 subterranean chambers of wonder and expansive landscaped gardens featuring a sparkling crystal cloud.
beschreibung:
Overview

The Swarovski Kristallwelten (Crystal Worlds) in Wattens near Innsbruck are among Austria's most iconic attractions, having delighted more than 16 million visitors since opening in 1995. Originally conceived by Austrian multimedia artist André Heller for the centenary of crystal manufacturer Swarovski, the site is guarded by the iconic plant-covered Giant spitting water into a pond. Deep inside the Giant's interior lie 18 underground Chambers of Wonder, where world-famous artists and architects such as Brian Eno, Zaha Hadid, and Yayoi Kusama have transformed crystal into mesmerizing sensory art installations. Outside, a 7.5-hectare landscaped garden blends contemporary art with pristine Alpine scenery.

Route & Requirements

Visitors follow a continuous walking route through 18 unique Chambers of Wonder, from the glittering Crystal Dome to the enchanting Silent Light installation. Outdoors, paved, barrier-free pathways wind through the expansive gardens. The showpiece of the garden is the massive Crystal Cloud by Cao Perrot, featuring over 800,000 hand-mounted crystals floating above a dark mirror pool. Families with children will appreciate the four-storey play tower, outdoor adventure playground, and green labyrinth. The entire site is fully accessible for strollers and wheelchair users. Allow about two to three hours for a fulfilling visit.

Visit & Arrival

Swarovski Crystal Worlds is open daily throughout the year (09:00 to 19:00, last admission at 18:00). Standard admission is around 25.00 Euro for adults and 9.00 Euro for children aged 6 to 17. By car, take the A12 motorway to the Wattens exit, where spacious free parking lots are located. A dedicated Swarovski Shuttle bus operates multiple times daily between Innsbruck Main Station and the attraction. Alternatively, regional trains (S-Bahn S4/S5) run regularly from Innsbruck to Fritzens-Wattens station.

Tips

Late afternoon is an ideal time to visit when sunlight illuminates the Crystal Cloud and evening lighting brings the Giant to life. Combine your tour with a meal or coffee at Daniels Kristallwelten restaurant, known for its fine in-house patisserie.
